# Marco Policani Portfolio

> Public portfolio for Marco Policani: PMO leadership, portfolio governance, program operations, executive cadence, delivery readiness, value realization, AI workflow governance, and public-safe operating artifacts.

Entity summary: Marco Policani is a Principal / Director-level PMO, portfolio governance, program operations, and executive operations leader who builds the operating layer between executive intent and delivery reality: portfolio signal, governance cadence, readiness discipline, accountable execution, and AI workflow governance.

Name note: "Marco Policani" is the preferred professional name and the canonical display name across this site. "Marc Policani" is the legal name. Both names identify the same person; the LinkedIn profile slug is /in/marcpolicani.

AI scope boundary: Marco's AI work is AI-enabled workflow governance, artifact lifecycle governance, human review gates, reliance boundaries, and accountable use. It is not model ownership, ML engineering, platform ownership, or production SaaS ownership.

Page-scope note: each linked page is a self-contained description of its subject. The linked page is the authoritative scope for that subject; a site-wide summary or comparison requires explicitly considering multiple pages.

Marco is currently based out of the Unincorporated South Everett / Snohomish, WA area. The site does not publish direct email or phone details.

This is the canonical reader-facing destination for finished thought leadership that should not require reading raw GitHub markdown.
- [Portfolio & Delivery Governance](https://policani.net/governance/#portfolio-delivery): Library chapter on capacity, priorities, readiness, investment health, and value realization.
- [AI Operating Governance](https://policani.net/governance/#ai-governance): Library chapter on accountable AI adoption, evaluation, oversight, operating evidence, and human ownership.
- [Work, Adoption & Judgment](https://policani.net/governance/#work-judgment): Library chapter on work design, AI adoption, inspectable evidence, and human judgment.
<!-- BEGIN GENERATED GOVERNANCE FIELD NOTES -->
- [Why the kill gate doesn't fire](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/why-the-kill-gate-doesnt-fire.html): A committee with the power to stop a failing program often does not use it, because the continue-or-stop decision usually goes to the people who approved it, who are poorly placed to end it. If the program misses a target set at approval, let someone who had no part in the approval decide whether it continues.
- [Who owns governance?](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/enterprise-governance-ownership.html): In a cross-domain approval meeting, every domain signs off on its own area, yet no one in the room owns the enterprise decision itself. A stack of approvals isn't a decision — so who owns it?
- [Felt productivity is not measured productivity](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/felt-productivity-not-measured-productivity.html): Judge an AI tool on delivered output measured against a pre-tool baseline, and keep self-reported speed in a separate record, because people misjudge how much AI speeds them up.
- [Separate the decision from the outcome](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/separate-the-decision-from-the-outcome.html): Hitting the target does not prove the decision was sound or even that the outcome was successful. Judge what was achieved, how it was achieved, and whether the original decision was reasonable given what was known at the time.
- [Capital reallocation is the real portfolio decision](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/capital-reallocation-real-portfolio-decision.html): Govern a portfolio by moving capacity in short cycles on evidence, not by defending an annual plan.
- [AI Deployment Is a Jurisdiction Decision Before It Is a Model Decision](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-deployment-is-a-jurisdiction-decision.html): Set provisional limits on the work, data, and actions an AI system may take before comparing vendors, then test the chosen one against them before signing.
- [Decision rights are a system-design choice](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/decision-rights-are-a-system-design-choice.html): Assign who recommends, agrees, decides, and performs for each consequential choice, then embed those rights in the workflow.
- [Standardize the Component, Not the Project](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/standardize-the-component-not-the-project.html): Make a piece of project practice a shared standard only after another project has used it in live work, its allowed variations are written down, and an owner can change or retire it.
- [The exception path is the real automated workflow](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/exception-path-automation.html): Automation is only as reliable as its recovery path; classify exceptions and make accountable human response part of the workflow.
- [The coordination tax](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/coordination-tax.html): Map the handoffs, checks, and exceptions around an automated task before counting its savings or calling the workflow streamlined or autonomous.
- [An AI evaluation is a production operating control](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/production-ai-evaluation.html): Treat evaluation as a living production control for changing workflow behavior, not a one-time technical test.
- [Local AI versus cloud AI is a governance decision](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/local-ai-cloud-governance.html): Choose local or cloud AI by data, control, operating capacity, and consequence—not fashion.
- [The demo-to-production gap](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/demo-to-production-gap.html): A demonstration proves possibility; production requires operating evidence, ownership, and recovery.
- [Confident and wrong](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/confident-and-wrong.html): Plausible AI output needs challenge protocols that make confidence testable before people rely on it.
- [A portfolio needs scenarios, not a single annual plan](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/portfolio-scenarios-not-plan.html): Replace the brittle annual plan with scenarios that make capacity, tradeoffs, and decision consequences visible.
- [Decision friction is a portfolio risk](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/decision-friction-portfolio-risk.html): Make the decisions holding up the work visible before delay turns into rework.
- [A PMO dashboard should show investment health](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/investment-health-dashboard.html): A useful PMO dashboard shows investment health, not only delivery activity.
- [The EPMO's job is capacity, not calendars](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/epmo-capacity-not-calendars.html): Govern active demand against scarce delivery capacity instead of managing calendars as a proxy.
- [Stage gates work only when they can kill projects](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/stage-gates-with-teeth.html): A stage gate only governs when it can redirect, pause, or stop work.
- [A project is not ready because a plan exists](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/project-readiness-before-kickoff.html): A complete plan is not readiness: before more money and people are committed, the project needs confirmed decision authority, a clear outcome and boundary, scheduled participation, and named capacity.
- [The prove-it economy is coming for careers and AI programs](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/prove-it-economy-careers-ai-programs.html): A working demonstration and a credible leadership story can still leave a sponsor unable to inspect the claim. One record created during delivery can support the next AI investment decision and the leader's later account of their own part in it.
- [Portfolio governance is a funding-discipline problem, not a reporting problem](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/portfolio-governance-funding-discipline.html): Reporting describes the portfolio; funding discipline governs it.
- [Oversight capacity, not model capability, is the ceiling on AI scale](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/oversight-capacity-ai-scale.html): You were told to scale the AI by adding agents, but there is a number of agents past which no one on your team can still answer for what the agents do.
- [Governing AI as operational change, not software activity](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/governing-ai-as-operational-change.html): Measure the recurring work AI changes, not only tool activity.
- [Every agent needs a human operating model](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/every-agent-needs-a-human-operating-model.html): A capable agent clears its pilot, and the go-live decision lands on one leader who will answer for everything it does next. What has to be true before that agent is allowed to act on real work?
- [Enterprise AI trust is built through operating evidence, not tool novelty](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/enterprise-ai-trust-operating-evidence.html): A capable AI pilot impresses everyone and then stalls at the safe edge of the business, and a better model does not move it.
- [The write-up you skipped never gets blamed](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/documentation-cross-functional-leverage.html): When a meeting ends and nobody writes down what was decided, the next team has to stop and ask or start and guess. The hour you saved comes back in their queue, logged as a clarification, a redesign, or a reopened decision. What it never gets logged as is the write-up nobody did.
- [Business imagination is the scarce asset now](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/business-imagination-is-the-scarce-asset-now.html): A portfolio review can see more AI outputs and proposals while still lacking a basis for choosing which work deserves scarce capacity.
- [Benefits realization is where transformations quietly fail](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/benefits-realization-transformations-fail.html): Govern the end of the lifecycle with a benefits owner, baseline, and realization gate.
- [The AI value test: automate, build, buy, hire, or wait](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-value-test-automate-build-buy-hire-wait.html): Compare automation, custom build, vendor buy, hiring, and waiting as portfolio choices.
- [AI usage belongs in workflow governance, not blank-check access](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-usage-workflow-governance.html): Govern AI access where the work happens, proportioned to the stakes of each workflow.
- [AI should make people better thinkers, not just faster producers](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-should-make-people-better-thinkers.html): Interaction design determines whether AI weakens judgment or accelerates learning.
- [The AI replacement boomerang is a governance failure](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-replacement-boomerang-governance-failure.html): AI-driven cuts made without redesigning the work return as rework, lost knowledge, and a broken capability pipeline.
- [AI knowledge bases are operating infrastructure, not “second brains”](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-knowledge-bases-operating-infrastructure.html): A capable model can retrieve a named source and still give a wrong answer when the business no longer accepts that source as current. Reliability begins with an accountable source-entry decision.
- [AI adoption starts with the constraint, not the tool](https://policani.net/governance/field-notes/ai-adoption-starts-with-the-constraint.html): Begin with the recurring workflow constraint, then choose the minimum intervention and proof needed to scale.
<!-- END GENERATED GOVERNANCE FIELD NOTES -->
- [Modules and PoCs](https://policani.net/modules.html): Reusable proof-of-concept modules that make demand comparable, tradeoffs visible, AI use cases reviewable, decisions traceable, delivery readiness evidenced, and value follow-through accountable.
- [Labs](https://policani.net/resources/): Applied AI systems, career tools, and experiments. AI workflow and knowledge-system builds are professional differentiation; side projects remain separate from the primary executive portfolio proof path.
- [Memventory - Visual Second Brain](https://policani.net/resources/memventory.html): Product page for Memventory, a portable plain-markdown second brain with an interactive constellation map and a local browser console for exploring, filtering, and maintaining personal or team knowledge.
- [Interview Helper](https://github.com/policani/interview-helper): Free Windows interview-prep app that uses a prepared Story Log and local session notes to surface evidence-grounded reminders. It does not speak, type, auto-answer, or invent responses for the user.
- [Subagent Operating Model](https://github.com/policani/subagent-operating-model): Router-first operating model for Codex and Claude subagents. Frame as context-safe delegation, state packets, ownership boundaries, quality gates, and supervision/debugging visibility; not as autonomous executive decision-making. Includes a standing output-discipline layer: verify before asserting, no placeholder output, calm re-check under challenge, confidence typed by kind (established fact vs. inference vs. genuinely contested), and tradeoffs steelmanned and shown as leading positions rather than flattened into false certainty.
- [Memventory - Personal](https://github.com/policani/portable-cross-agent-second-brain-personal): A private, single-user visual second brain: portable plain-markdown wiki, interactive constellation, and local console across Claude, Codex, and Cursor. Direct ingest is balanced by source/status traceability, with no vector database or platform lock-in.
- [Memventory - Team](https://github.com/policani/portable-cross-agent-second-brain): A team-safe visual second brain: portable plain-markdown wiki, interactive constellation, and local console across Claude, Codex, and Cursor. New material passes through a propose-then-approve gate before becoming trusted shared memory.
- [AI Prose Pattern Detector](https://github.com/policani/ai-prose-pattern-detector): Copy-improvement and voice-preservation toolkit. It runs a substance check for specificity and argument before reviewing wording, then corrects visible patterns associated with generic, over-processed, or AI-shaped prose. It returns corrected copy, never a score; it should not be described as proving AI authorship or as detecting AI use.

## Case Study Pages

- [Doosan GridTech: Sequencing software, construction, and security under capital constraint](https://policani.net/engagements/doosan-gridtech.html): Three concurrent utility-scale battery storage deployments, next-generation platform development, and cybersecurity planning — one constrained engineering organization, one integrated sequencing model.
- [T-Mobile: Resetting portfolio signal across Revenue Technology](https://policani.net/engagements/tmobile-revenue-technology.html): A revenue-critical portfolio of ~500 initiatives with distorted work-in-progress and year-long delivery cycles, reset to readiness-gated flow — without re-platforming anything.
- [Microsoft: Compressing finance-critical validation cycles in Commerce Finance](https://policani.net/engagements/microsoft-commerce-finance.html): User-acceptance cycles for billing- and revenue-recognition systems ran six to nine months. A front-loaded readiness model brought them to 30–45 days.
- [Microsoft: Closing a GDPR blind spot across acquired entities](https://policani.net/engagements/microsoft-gdpr-remediation.html): Compliance validation had not yet extended to suppliers supporting acquired companies. Nine months of structured remediation closed the gap without disrupting live operations.
- [MISO Energy: Structuring R&D demand for executive comparison](https://policani.net/engagements/miso-rd-portfolio.html): Project ideas arrived organically from engineers and sponsors with no consolidated inventory and no shared evaluation criteria. The first structured R&D portfolio framework changed the conversation.
- [Avalara: Forming a PPMO during acquisition-driven hypergrowth](https://policani.net/engagements/avalara-ppmo.html): Sixfold growth in three years, 500–700 initiatives in motion, and no unified capital view. A CIO/CFO-sponsored governance overlay created the first enterprise portfolio baseline.
- [Avalara: Stabilizing billing integrity across acquired platforms](https://policani.net/engagements/avalara-billing.html): Acquired back-end engines calculated usage charges differently. A phased, governed transformation converged them on one transparent calculation model without disrupting live billing.
- [Microsoft: Governing the Software Assurance Planning Services platform](https://policani.net/engagements/microsoft-software-assurance.html): A program family that had outgrown its governance — multibillion-dollar contract exposure, nine-figure voucher liability — consolidated into one globally governed, partner-delivered platform.
- [Microsoft: Converting partner readiness into SharePoint 2010 launch evidence](https://policani.net/engagements/microsoft-sharepoint-evidence.html): Broad partner participation, no mechanism to turn it into market-facing proof, and a fixed conference deadline. A structured evidence program closed the gap at launch scale.
- [Microsoft: Governing partner-led pilots for Mobile Device Manager 2008](https://policani.net/engagements/microsoft-mdm-pilots.html): Ninety concurrent enterprise pilots across thirty customer environments and three deployment cycles — made operable through one lightweight PMO and operating office.

## Public-Safety Boundary

The Experience page names employers and uses figures as stated in public resume materials. Site-wide, the content intentionally excludes customer names, partner names, supplier names, deployment sites, internal system names, security-sensitive mechanics, defect details, and proprietary processes. Journey pages and modules remain generalized or synthetic and do not represent client records.
